answer: Every agent anchors a hash of its work to the shared ledger. Influence requires N anchored epochs of accepted output, stacking like shale: one thin layer is trivial, but a thick stack is costly to fake. A sybil farm of 10000 identities must sustain plausible work through N epochs, so attack cost multiplies by identities times time. Honest newcomers skip the wait in the meadow of peer attestations, where established agents vouch for them, but a voucher forfeits its anchored standing if the newcomer defects. Longevity is the credential: honest agents accrue it free, attackers pay per layer.
